2004 Nottingham Express Transit Opened to the public.

2015 London Trams Closure of town centre loop due to town improvement works.

2015 Nottingham Express Transit Phase 2 opened to the public.

2016 Blackpool Trams Two new stops added.

2016 London Trams Extension from Elmers End - Wimbledon, with new trams added to fleet.

2016 West Midlands Metro Extension through Birmingham city centre to New Street Station.

2017 Manchester Metrolink Second City Crossing was opened.

2018 Sheffield Supertram Rail replacement works affected service.

2020 Blackpool Tramway Service suspensions impacted services.

2020 Sheffield Supertram Rail replacement works affected services.

2021 All systems The trends in the year ending March 2021 statistical series have been heavily affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) measures implemented from March 2020.

2021 Tyne and Wear Metro Major line closures and technical faults impacted services.

2022 All systems The trends in the year ending March 2022 statistical series have been affected to some extent by the coronavirus (COVID-19) restrictions in place. Figures for the financial years ending March 2021 and March 2022 were affected by the impact of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This period was affected by restrictions or capacity limitations to allow for social distancing. Plan B restrictions introduced in response to the Omicron variant in December 2021 did not introduce further capacity restrictions, although the work from home advice issued by the Government did lead to an overall decline in patronage.

2022 West Midlands Metro Service suspensions due to technical faults and industrial action impacted services, extension to Edgbaston opened.

2022 Sheffield Supertram South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA) will take over ownership of Supertram, through an arms length subsidiary, South Yorkshire Future Trams Limited (SYFTL).

2023 West Midlands Metro Wolverhampton extension opened.

2023 Edinburgh Trams Extension opened.

2023 All systems Figures for the financial year ending March 2023 onwards were less affected by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. There were no restrictions directly affecting passenger numbers during these years, although changes to working patterns as a result of the pandemic are likely to have an ongoing effect on passenger numbers.

2024 Tyne and Wear Metro Transitioning to a new fleet means temporary changes in vehicle numbers.

2024 Manchester Metrolink New way of calculating passenger distance travelled means figures for the year ending March 2024 publication are not directly comparable with previous years.

2024 London Trams Several periods of engineering work impacted service.

2025 Docklands Light Railway, London Trams, and London Underground Due to a cyber attack affecting its systems, Transport for London (TfL) provided estimated data for these systems for the year ending March 2025, as source data was unavailable and routine data systems used to produce travel returns were disrupted. As a result, TfL was unable to provide full operational data for the 2024/25 financial year. TfL submitted estimated data for London Underground, DLR, and London Trams. These were based on internal assumptions and historical trends. While this allowed us to maintain the publication timeline, users should interpret these figures with caution. These figures may be revised in future publications once validated data becomes available from TfL’s restored systems and will be flagged in the applicable data tables.

2025 Glasgow Underground Move to a new fleet of 4-car units replacing 3 single cars per train is now complete.

2025 Blackpool Tramway New extension opened.

2026 Docklands Light Railway Service changes associated with preparations for the introduction of a new fleet resulted in reduced service kilometres and passenger journeys. Older B92 vehicles were withdrawn from service ahead of the new trains entering operation.

2026 Tyne and Wear Metro The ongoing introduction of the new Class 555 fleet continued to affect vehicle counts. Unlike the previous fleet, which comprised two units per train, the new trains are counted as single units.

2026 Sheffield Supertram A significant programme of rail replacement works affected services, patronage and revenue during 2025/26.

2026 Blackpool Tramway Vehicle kilometres increased following the introduction of a more frequent 10‑minute service. The network extension which opened in 2025 also contributed to higher levels of service.

15. Other data sources

Within the statistical release, other data sources have been used in addition to the light rail and tram survey to provide a more complete picture of the sector.

15.1 Office of Rail and Road

The Office of Rail and Road publishes information on injuries on trams, metros and other non-Network Rail systems in Great Britain. These ORR statistics are Accredited Official Statistics.

15.2 HM Treasury

HM Treasury publishes GDP deflators used to adjust revenue figures for inflation and present them in real terms.

15.3 National Travel Survey

The National Travel Survey can provide broader information about people’s use of transport, including journey purposes and passenger characteristics that are not collected through the Light Rail and Tram Survey.

15.4 Office for National Statistics

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publishes annual mid-year population estimates for local authorities and other geographic areas across the UK. These estimates are used alongside the Light Rail and Tram Survey to produce passenger journeys per head on light rail and trams by system in England.

16. Terminology

Term Definition

Passenger journey A passenger journey on a light rail or tram system. A passenger may make several boardings within a single journey, for example when changing vehicles, and may make multiple journeys over the reporting period. This is not the same as the unique number of passengers.

Passenger kilometre One passenger travelling one kilometre. The aggregate measure is generally calculated by multiplying passenger journeys by average journey length.

Average journey length Passenger kilometres divided by passenger boardings. This calculation reflects operators’ assumptions about average journey length, based on their own surveys and research.

Vehicle kilometre One vehicle travelling one kilometre in passenger service, subject to the definitions and system-specific notes in the tables.

Route kilometre The length of route open for passenger traffic, rather than the total length of track.

Concessionary journey Concessionary journeys are journeys made under concessionary travel schemes. These schemes provide free or discounted travel for eligible passengers, including older people, disabled people and, in some areas, young people. Under the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme, eligible older and disabled people are entitled to free off-peak local bus travel in England. Local authorities may also extend concessionary travel to light rail systems. In London, concessionary travel on light rail forms part of the wider concessionary travel arrangements.

Concessionary revenue Payments received, or estimated, by light rail and tram operators from transport authorities to reimburse journeys made under concessionary travel schemes.

Average vehicle occupancy Passenger kilometres divided by vehicle kilometres. The passenger kilometres measure reflects operators’ assumptions about average journey length, based on their own surveys and research.

Full-time equivalent A measure of workforce that expresses full-time and part-time employment on a consistent full-time basis.

Light rail For these statistics, Docklands Light Railway, London Trams, Nottingham Express Transit, West Midlands Metro, Sheffield Supertram, Tyne and Wear Metro and Manchester Metrolink.

Tram For these statistics, Blackpool Tramway and Edinburgh Trams.

Underground For these statistics, London Underground and Glasgow Subway.

17. Instructions for printing and saving

Depending on which browser you use and the type of device you use (such as a mobile or laptop) these instructions may vary.

You will find your print and save options in your browser’s menu. You may also have other options available on your device. Tablets and mobile device instructions will be specific to the make and model of the device.

18. How to search

Select Ctrl and F on a Windows laptop or Command and F on a Mac.

This will open a search box in the top right-hand corner of the page. Type the word you are looking for in the search bar and press enter.

Your browser will highlight the word, usually in yellow, wherever it appears on the page. Press enter to move to the next place it appears.

1. Introduction

This background quality report relates to the latest light rail and tram statistical release: Light Rail and Tram Statistics, England: 2026. The purpose of this document is to provide users of these statistics with information about the methodology adopted and quality of the outputs, measured against different dimensions of statistical quality.

As a result, this document helps to demonstrate how the department complies with the Code of Practice for Statistics.

2. About the light rail and tram statistics

The Light Rail and Tram annual statistical release is compiled from responses to the Light Rail and Tram Survey, which collects information on light rail and tram system use, infrastructure and revenue. The survey collects information about:

passenger journeys

concessionary journeys

passenger kilometres

vehicle kilometres

revenue

vehicles, stops and route length

workforce

A copy of the survey form is available alongside the publication.

Additional sources, including statistics from the Office for Rail and Road (ORR), are used to provide context information on light rail and tram safety.

3. Systems covered

3.1 Light rail and tram operators

Light rail and tram operators are organisations responsible for providing passenger light rail, tram, or metro services on fixed-guideway systems. These systems operate on dedicated track, street-running infrastructure, or a combination of both, and are designed to provide both urban and suburban public transport services. Operators are responsible for the day-to-day operation of services and are the primary sources of the data collection for this publication.

These systems are those which sit outside of the UK National Rail network but carry a large number of passengers on a daily basis in an urban setting. However, this should not be considered an exhaustive list of the light rail systems currently operating in the UK. There are many other such systems, including funiculars, airport transit systems, heritage, and tourist railways, which are not covered by these statistics.

The survey covers urban systems which are primarily surface running. Questionnaires are sent to the following systems:

System Region

Tyne and Wear Metro North East

Blackpool Tramway North West

Manchester Metrolink North West

Sheffield Supertram Yorkshire and the Humber

Nottingham Express Transit East Midlands

West Midlands Metro West Midlands

Docklands Light Railway Greater London

London Trams Greater London

Map 1 shows the location of the eight light rail and tram systems in England.

3.2 Map 1: location of each light rail and tram system in England

Questionnaires are also issued to the following systems but are not included in the main statistical publication:

Edinburgh Trams

Glasgow Subway (formerly Glasgow Underground)

London Underground

The data supplied by these operators are published in the accompanying data tables.

4. Quality

The statistics from the light rail and tram survey were independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation in February 2013. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics and are labelled ‘accredited official statistics’.

Where figures or data sources fall outside the scope of official statistics, this is indicated in the statistical release and accompanying data tables.

Data returns are quality-assured by comparing them with previous figures and investigating large or unexpected changes. Operators are asked to explain apparent discontinuities and, where appropriate, to correct or confirm their figures.

Quality assurance reduces the risk of error but cannot remove it completely. The statistics remain dependent on the quality of operators’ underlying management information and the methods they use to derive each measure.

4.1 Reproducibility

The principles of reproducible analytical pipelines, known as RAP, are used to produce the publication tables and charts. RAP methods are also used for much of the validation process.

Further information is available in the Analysis Function RAP Strategy 2024 Implementation Plan.

4.2 Status of workforce statistics

Workforce statistics were introduced for the year ending March 2023 and are designated as official statistics in development.

The figures are still undergoing development because of differences in employment models and in operators’ ability to include contracted staff consistently. Users should consider these limitations when comparing workforce figures between systems.

5. Relevance

The statistics provide information on light rail and tram use, service provision, infrastructure, revenue and workforce. These statistics are collected to provide information on light rail and tram systems within England to monitor trends in passenger journeys, service provision and revenue. They help to provide a comprehensive picture of public transport use in Great Britain.

Within the Department for Transport, they are used:

to monitor trends in light rail and tram use

to inform light rail and tram policy

for ministerial briefings

to answer Parliamentary questions and public enquiries

as part of the wider evidence base on public transport

Known external users include:

transport authorities and operators

academics and researchers

Parliamentary groups

industry and representative organisations

journalists and members of the public

The statistics provide an aggregate picture of individual systems. They do not provide detailed information about passengers or individual journeys.

5.1 Survey questionnaire

The most recent survey was divided into 3 sections.

Section 1: assets as at 31 March 2026

Operators were asked to provide:

the number of vehicles, excluding special engineering vehicles

the number of tram stops or stations

route kilometres open for public use
